# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility

## Overview

This feature provides a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs suitable for identifiers, filenames, and web URLs. The function normalizes text by converting it to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing special characters, and ensuring clean hyphen formatting.

## Business Context

URL-safe slugs are a common requirement in web applications, content management systems, and data processing pipelines. A standardized slugify utility ensures consistent identifier generation across the codebase and reduces the risk of invalid characters in URLs, filenames, or database keys.

## Functional Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to convert input text to lowercase so that slugs are case-insensitive and consistent.

**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization prevents duplicate identifiers that differ only in case (e.g., "Hello" vs "hello") and follows standard URL slug conventions.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case conversion
- Example: "HELLO World" → "hello-world"

### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: As a developer, I need spaces and underscores in the input text to be replaced with hyphens so that slugs use a consistent word separator.

**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs and provide better readability than underscores or encoded spaces (%20).

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- All space characters (including multiple consecutive spaces) are replaced with hyphens
- All underscore characters are replaced with hyphens
- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
- Example: "hello  world" → "hello-world"
- Example: "foo__bar" → "foo-bar"

### REQ-003: Special Character Removal (Must Have)
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: As a developer, I need special characters and punctuation to be removed from the slug so that the output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens.

**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, filenames, and database identifiers. Limiting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures broad compatibility.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) are retained in the output
- All other characters (punctuation, symbols, etc.) are removed
- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world"
- Example: "user@email.com" → "useremailcom"

### REQ-004: Hyphen Normalization (Must Have)
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: As a developer, I need multiple consecutive hyphens to be collapsed into a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.

**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can result from the combination of whitespace replacement and special character removal.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Any sequence of 2 or more consecutive hyphens is replaced with a single hyphen
- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
- Example: "hello--world" → "hello-world"

### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: As a developer, I need leading and trailing hyphens to be removed from the slug so that the output starts and ends with alphanumeric characters.

**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at the beginning or end of input text and create invalid or unprofessional-looking identifiers.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Any hyphens at the start of the slug are removed
- Any hyphens at the end of the slug are removed
- Internal hyphens (between words) are preserved
- Example: "-hello-world-" → "hello-world"
- Example: "  foo bar  " → "foo-bar" (spaces become hyphens, then trimmed)

### REQ-006: Empty Input Handling (Must Have)
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to handle empty or whitespace-only input predictably so that the application doesn't fail when processing edge cases.

**Rationale**: Empty input or input consisting only of special characters could result in an empty slug after processing, which needs to be handled gracefully.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Empty string input returns an empty string
- Input consisting only of whitespace returns an empty string
- Input consisting only of special characters returns an empty string
- Example: "" → ""
- Example: "   " → ""
- Example: "!!!" → ""

## User Stories

### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title
**As a** content management system developer
**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
**So that** articles have clean, readable URLs without manual slug creation

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- **GIVEN** an article title like "10 Best Practices for TypeScript"
- **WHEN** I call `slugify("10 Best Practices for TypeScript")`
- **THEN** I receive "10-best-practices-for-typescript"

### STORY-002: Create Filename from User Input
**As a** file processing system developer
**I want** to sanitize user-provided names into valid filenames
**So that** files can be saved without filesystem errors

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- **GIVEN** user input like "My Document (Final).txt"
- **WHEN** I call `slugify("My Document (Final)")`
- **THEN** I receive "my-document-final" suitable for a filename

### STORY-003: Generate Database Identifier
**As a** database system developer
**I want** to create unique identifiers from human-readable names
**So that** records have consistent, predictable keys

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- **GIVEN** a category name like "Home & Garden"
- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Home & Garden")`
- **THEN** I receive "home-garden" suitable as a database key

## Test Scenarios

| Scenario | Input | Expected Output |
|----------|-------|-----------------|
| Basic text | "Hello World" | "hello-world" |
| With punctuation | "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" |
| Multiple spaces | "foo  bar" | "foo-bar" |

    16→

    21→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)

    27→

    33→

**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft

## Summary

Implement a pure `slugify` function in `src/utils.ts` that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs using a chain of string transformations: lowercase conversion, whitespace/underscore replacement with hyphens, special character removal, hyphen collapse, and edge trimming. flowchart LR
    Input["Input String"] --> Lower["toLowerCase()"]
    Lower --> Replace["Replace spaces/underscores with hyphens"]

    Collapse --> Trim["Trim leading/trailing hyphens"]
    Trim --> Output["Output Slug"]

| D2 | Transformation order | lowercase -> replace spaces/underscores -> remove special chars -> collapse hyphens -> trim | Logical pipeline where each step builds on previous; trimming last ensures clean output | Different ordering could produce different intermediate states but same result |

| D4 | Hyphen collapse pattern | `/--+/g` | Matches two or more consecutive hyphens for replacement with single; more efficient than repeated single replacement | While loop with single replacement (slower), recursive approach (unnecessary complexity) |
| D5 | Edge trimming approach | Regex `/^-+|-+$/g` | Single regex handles both leading and trailing in one pass | Separate trim operations, substring manipulation (more verbose) |

    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→This feature provides a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs suitable for identifiers, filenames, and web URLs. The function normalizes text by converting it to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing special characters, and ensuring clean hyphen formatting.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→URL-safe slugs are a common requirement in web applications, content management systems, and data processing pipelines. A standardized slugify utility ensures consistent identifier generation across the codebase and reduces the risk of invalid characters in URLs, filenames, or database keys.
    18→
    19→## Functional Requirements
    20→
    21→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
    22→**Priority**: Must Have
    23→**User Type**: Developer
    24→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to convert input text to lowercase so that slugs are case-insensitive and consistent.
    25→
    26→**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization prevents duplicate identifiers that differ only in case (e.g., "Hello" vs "hello") and follows standard URL slug conventions.
    27→
    28→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    29→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    30→- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
    31→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case conversion
    32→- Example: "HELLO World" → "hello-world"
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
    35→**Priority**: Must Have
    36→**User Type**: Developer
    37→**Description**: As a developer, I need spaces and underscores in the input text to be replaced with hyphens so that slugs use a consistent word separator.
    38→
    39→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs and provide better readability than underscores or encoded spaces (%20).
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- All space characters (including multiple consecutive spaces) are replaced with hyphens
    43→- All underscore characters are replaced with hyphens
    44→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
    45→- Example: "hello  world" → "hello-world"
    46→- Example: "foo__bar" → "foo-bar"
    47→
    48→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal (Must Have)
    49→**Priority**: Must Have
    50→**User Type**: Developer
    51→**Description**: As a developer, I need special characters and punctuation to be removed from the slug so that the output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens.
    52→
    53→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, filenames, and database identifiers. Limiting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures broad compatibility.
    54→
    55→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    56→- Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) are retained in the output
    57→- All other characters (punctuation, symbols, etc.) are removed
    58→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world"
    59→- Example: "user@email.com" → "useremailcom"
    60→
    61→### REQ-004: Hyphen Normalization (Must Have)
    62→**Priority**: Must Have
    63→**User Type**: Developer
    64→**Description**: As a developer, I need multiple consecutive hyphens to be collapsed into a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.
    65→
    66→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can result from the combination of whitespace replacement and special character removal.
    67→
    68→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    69→- Any sequence of 2 or more consecutive hyphens is replaced with a single hyphen
    70→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
    71→- Example: "hello--world" → "hello-world"
    72→
    73→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
    74→**Priority**: Must Have
    75→**User Type**: Developer
    76→**Description**: As a developer, I need leading and trailing hyphens to be removed from the slug so that the output starts and ends with alphanumeric characters.
    77→
    78→**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at the beginning or end of input text and create invalid or unprofessional-looking identifiers.
    79→
    80→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    81→- Any hyphens at the start of the slug are removed
    82→- Any hyphens at the end of the slug are removed
    83→- Internal hyphens (between words) are preserved
    84→- Example: "-hello-world-" → "hello-world"
    85→- Example: "  foo bar  " → "foo-bar" (spaces become hyphens, then trimmed)
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Empty Input Handling (Must Have)
    88→**Priority**: Must Have
    89→**User Type**: Developer

    91→
    92→**Rationale**: Empty input or input consisting only of special characters could result in an empty slug after processing, which needs to be handled gracefully.
    93→
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Empty string input returns an empty string
    96→- Input consisting only of whitespace returns an empty string
    97→- Input consisting only of special characters returns an empty string
    98→- Example: "" → ""
    99→- Example: "   " → ""

     8→
     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→This feature provides a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs suitable for identifiers, filenames, and web URLs. The function normalizes text by converting it to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing special characters, and ensuring clean hyphen formatting.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→URL-safe slugs are a common requirement in web applications, content management systems, and data processing pipelines. A standardized slugify utility ensures consistent identifier generation across the codebase and reduces the risk of invalid characters in URLs, filenames, or database keys.
    18→
    19→## Functional Requirements
    20→
    21→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
    22→**Priority**: Must Have
    23→**User Type**: Developer
    24→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to convert input text to lowercase so that slugs are case-insensitive and consistent.
    25→
    26→**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization prevents duplicate identifiers that differ only in case (e.g., "Hello" vs "hello") and follows standard URL slug conventions.
    27→
    28→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    29→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    30→- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
    31→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case conversion
    32→- Example: "HELLO World" → "hello-world"
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
    35→**Priority**: Must Have
    36→**User Type**: Developer
    37→**Description**: As a developer, I need spaces and underscores in the input text to be replaced with hyphens so that slugs use a consistent word separator.
    38→
    39→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs and provide better readability than underscores or encoded spaces (%20).
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- All space characters (including multiple consecutive spaces) are replaced with hyphens
    43→- All underscore characters are replaced with hyphens
    44→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
    45→- Example: "hello  world" → "hello-world"
    46→- Example: "foo__bar" → "foo-bar"
    47→
    48→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal (Must Have)
    49→**Priority**: Must Have
    50→**User Type**: Developer
    51→**Description**: As a developer, I need special characters and punctuation to be removed from the slug so that the output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens.
    52→
    53→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, filenames, and database identifiers. Limiting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures broad compatibility.
    54→
    55→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    56→- Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) are retained in the output
    57→- All other characters (punctuation, symbols, etc.) are removed
    58→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world"
    59→- Example: "user@email.com" → "useremailcom"
    60→
    61→### REQ-004: Hyphen Normalization (Must Have)
    62→**Priority**: Must Have
    63→**User Type**: Developer
    64→**Description**: As a developer, I need multiple consecutive hyphens to be collapsed into a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.
    65→
    66→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can result from the combination of whitespace replacement and special character removal.
    67→
    68→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    69→- Any sequence of 2 or more consecutive hyphens is replaced with a single hyphen
    70→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
    71→- Example: "hello--world" → "hello-world"
    72→
    73→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
    74→**Priority**: Must Have
    75→**User Type**: Developer
    76→**Description**: As a developer, I need leading and trailing hyphens to be removed from the slug so that the output starts and ends with alphanumeric characters.
    77→
    78→**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at the beginning or end of input text and create invalid or unprofessional-looking identifiers.
    79→
    80→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    81→- Any hyphens at the start of the slug are removed
    82→- Any hyphens at the end of the slug are removed
    83→- Internal hyphens (between words) are preserved
    84→- Example: "-hello-world-" → "hello-world"
    85→- Example: "  foo bar  " → "foo-bar" (spaces become hyphens, then trimmed)
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Empty Input Handling (Must Have)
    88→**Priority**: Must Have
    89→**User Type**: Developer
    90→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to handle empty or whitespace-only input predictably so that the application doesn't fail when processing edge cases.
    91→
    92→**Rationale**: Empty input or input consisting only of special characters could result in an empty slug after processing, which needs to be handled gracefully.
    93→
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Empty string input returns an empty string
    96→- Input consisting only of whitespace returns an empty string
    97→- Input consisting only of special characters returns an empty string
    98→- Example: "" → ""
    99→- Example: "   " → ""
   100→- Example: "!!!" → ""
   101→
   102→## User Stories
   103→
   104→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title
   105→**As a** content management system developer
   106→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   107→**So that** articles have clean, readable URLs without manual slug creation
   108→
   109→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   110→- **GIVEN** an article title like "10 Best Practices for TypeScript"
   111→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("10 Best Practices for TypeScript")`
   112→- **THEN** I receive "10-best-practices-for-typescript"
   113→
   114→### STORY-002: Create Filename from User Input
   115→**As a** file processing system developer
   116→**I want** to sanitize user-provided names into valid filenames
   117→**So that** files can be saved without filesystem errors
   118→
   119→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   120→- **GIVEN** user input like "My Document (Final).txt"
   121→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("My Document (Final)")`
   122→- **THEN** I receive "my-document-final" suitable for a filename
   123→
   124→### STORY-003: Generate Database Identifier
   125→**As a** database system developer
   126→**I want** to create unique identifiers from human-readable names
   127→**So that** records have consistent, predictable keys
   128→
   129→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   130→- **GIVEN** a category name like "Home & Garden"
   131→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Home & Garden")`
   132→- **THEN** I receive "home-garden" suitable as a database key
   133→
   134→## Test Scenarios
   135→
   136→| Scenario | Input | Expected Output |
   137→|----------|-------|-----------------|
   138→| Basic text | "Hello World" | "hello-world" |
   139→| With punctuation | "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" |
   140→| Multiple spaces | "foo  bar" | "foo-bar" |
   141→| Underscores | "foo__bar" | "foo-bar" |

/**
 * Add two numbers.
 */
export function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  return a + b;
}

/**
 * Converts arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs.
 *
 * Transforms input by:
 * - Converting to lowercase
 * - Replacing spaces and underscores with hyphens
 * - Removing special characters (keeping only alphanumeric and hyphens)
 * - Collapsing consecutive hyphens
 * - Trimming leading and trailing hyphens
 *
 * @param input - The text to convert to a slug
 * @returns A URL-safe slug string, or empty string if input is empty/invalid
 */
export function slugify(input: string): string {
  return input
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[\s_]+/g, '-')
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, '')
    .replace(/-+/g, '-')
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '');
}

     8→
     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→This feature provides a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs suitable for identifiers, filenames, and web URLs. The function normalizes text by converting it to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing special characters, and ensuring clean hyphen formatting.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→URL-safe slugs are a common requirement in web applications, content management systems, and data processing pipelines. A standardized slugify utility ensures consistent identifier generation across the codebase and reduces the risk of invalid characters in URLs, filenames, or database keys.
    18→
    19→## Functional Requirements
    20→
    21→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
    22→**Priority**: Must Have
    23→**User Type**: Developer
    24→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to convert input text to lowercase so that slugs are case-insensitive and consistent.
    25→
    26→**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization prevents duplicate identifiers that differ only in case (e.g., "Hello" vs "hello") and follows standard URL slug conventions.
    27→
    28→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    29→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    30→- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
    31→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case conversion
    32→- Example: "HELLO World" → "hello-world"
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
    35→**Priority**: Must Have
    36→**User Type**: Developer
    37→**Description**: As a developer, I need spaces and underscores in the input text to be replaced with hyphens so that slugs use a consistent word separator.
    38→
    39→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs and provide better readability than underscores or encoded spaces (%20).
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- All space characters (including multiple consecutive spaces) are replaced with hyphens
    43→- All underscore characters are replaced with hyphens
    44→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
    45→- Example: "hello  world" → "hello-world"
    46→- Example: "foo__bar" → "foo-bar"
    47→
    48→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal (Must Have)
    49→**Priority**: Must Have
    50→**User Type**: Developer
    51→**Description**: As a developer, I need special characters and punctuation to be removed from the slug so that the output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens.
    52→
    53→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, filenames, and database identifiers. Limiting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures broad compatibility.
    54→
    55→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    56→- Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) are retained in the output
    57→- All other characters (punctuation, symbols, etc.) are removed
    58→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world"
    59→- Example: "user@email.com" → "useremailcom"
    60→
    61→### REQ-004: Hyphen Normalization (Must Have)
    62→**Priority**: Must Have
    63→**User Type**: Developer
    64→**Description**: As a developer, I need multiple consecutive hyphens to be collapsed into a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.
    65→
    66→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can result from the combination of whitespace replacement and special character removal.
    67→
    68→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    69→- Any sequence of 2 or more consecutive hyphens is replaced with a single hyphen
    70→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
    71→- Example: "hello--world" → "hello-world"
    72→
    73→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
    74→**Priority**: Must Have
    75→**User Type**: Developer
    76→**Description**: As a developer, I need leading and trailing hyphens to be removed from the slug so that the output starts and ends with alphanumeric characters.
    77→
    78→**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at the beginning or end of input text and create invalid or unprofessional-looking identifiers.
    79→
    80→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    81→- Any hyphens at the start of the slug are removed
    82→- Any hyphens at the end of the slug are removed
    83→- Internal hyphens (between words) are preserved
    84→- Example: "-hello-world-" → "hello-world"
    85→- Example: "  foo bar  " → "foo-bar" (spaces become hyphens, then trimmed)
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Empty Input Handling (Must Have)
    88→**Priority**: Must Have
    89→**User Type**: Developer
    90→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to handle empty or whitespace-only input predictably so that the application doesn't fail when processing edge cases.
    91→
    92→**Rationale**: Empty input or input consisting only of special characters could result in an empty slug after processing, which needs to be handled gracefully.
    93→
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Empty string input returns an empty string
    96→- Input consisting only of whitespace returns an empty string
    97→- Input consisting only of special characters returns an empty string
    98→- Example: "" → ""
    99→- Example: "   " → ""
   100→- Example: "!!!" → ""
   101→
   102→## User Stories
   103→
   104→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title
   105→**As a** content management system developer
   106→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   107→**So that** articles have clean, readable URLs without manual slug creation
   108→
   109→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   110→- **GIVEN** an article title like "10 Best Practices for TypeScript"
   111→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("10 Best Practices for TypeScript")`
   112→- **THEN** I receive "10-best-practices-for-typescript"
   113→
   114→### STORY-002: Create Filename from User Input
   115→**As a** file processing system developer
   116→**I want** to sanitize user-provided names into valid filenames
   117→**So that** files can be saved without filesystem errors
   118→
   119→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   120→- **GIVEN** user input like "My Document (Final).txt"
   121→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("My Document (Final)")`
   122→- **THEN** I receive "my-document-final" suitable for a filename
   123→
   124→### STORY-003: Generate Database Identifier
   125→**As a** database system developer
   126→**I want** to create unique identifiers from human-readable names
   127→**So that** records have consistent, predictable keys
   128→
   129→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   130→- **GIVEN** a category name like "Home & Garden"
   131→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Home & Garden")`
   132→- **THEN** I receive "home-garden" suitable as a database key
   133→
   134→## Test Scenarios
   135→
   136→| Scenario | Input | Expected Output |
   137→|----------|-------|-----------------|
   138→| Basic text | "Hello World" | "hello-world" |
   139→| With punctuation | "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" |
   140→| Multiple spaces | "foo  bar" | "foo-bar" |
   141→| Underscores | "foo__bar" | "foo-bar" |
   142→| Leading/trailing spaces | "  foo bar  " | "foo-bar" |
   143→| Multiple hyphens | "a---b" | "a-b" |
   144→| Mixed case | "CamelCaseText" | "camelcasetext" |
   145→| Numbers | "test123" | "test123" |
   146→| Special characters | "user@email.com" | "useremailcom" |
   147→| Empty string | "" | "" |
   148→| Only spaces | "   " | "" |
   149→| Only special chars | "!!!" | "" |
   150→
   151→## Non-Functional Requirements
   152→
   153→### NFR-001: Performance
   154→The function should process typical input strings (< 1000 characters) in under 1ms on modern hardware.
   155→
   156→### NFR-002: Compatibility
   157→The function should work with standard JavaScript/TypeScript string types and return standard string output.
   158→
   159→### NFR-003: Testability
   160→The function should be a pure function (no side effects) that is easily testable with standard testing frameworks.
   161→
   162→## Out of Scope
   163→
   164→The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
   165→
   166→- Unicode character transliteration (e.g., "café" → "cafe")
   167→- Locale-specific character handling
   168→- Custom slug patterns or configurations
   169→- Maximum length enforcement
   170→- Uniqueness validation or collision detection
   171→- Persistence or caching of generated slugs
   172→
   173→## Dependencies
   174→
   175→- TypeScript/JavaScript runtime environment
   176→- String manipulation capabilities (standard library)
   177→
   178→## AFK Mode Decisions
   179→
   180→**AFK Mode**: Enabled
   181→
   182→The following decisions were made automatically based on project context:
   183→
   184→### Decision 1: PRD Association
   185→**Point**: PRD selection
   186→**Choice**: No PRD associated
   187→**Rationale**: No PRD documents found in `/tmp/rp1-evals/4b3c8c55/workspace/.rp1/work/prds/`. This appears to be a standalone utility feature request.
   188→
   189→### Decision 2: Character Set Scope
   190→**Point**: Allowed character definition
   191→**Choice**: ASCII alphanumeric (a-z, 0-9) and hyphens only
   192→**Rationale**: The requirement specified "letter, number, or hyphen" without mentioning Unicode support. For a utility project, ASCII-only scope is the conservative default to avoid complexity around Unicode normalization and character classification.
   193→
   194→### Decision 3: Empty Result Handling
   195→**Point**: Behavior when all characters are removed
   196→**Choice**: Return empty string
   197→**Rationale**: No specific error handling was requested. Returning an empty string is the natural result of the specified transformation rules and allows calling code to decide how to handle empty slugs.
   198→
   199→### Decision 4: Module Location
   200→**Point**: Implementation location
   201→**Choice**: Add to existing `src/utils.ts` module
   202→**Rationale**: The KB describes `src/utils.ts` as the location for "pure functions providing reusable logic," which matches the slugify function's nature. This maintains consistency with existing project structure.
   203→
   204→### Decision 5: Edge Case - Only Hyphens
   205→**Point**: Input that becomes only hyphens (e.g., "---")
   206→**Choice**: Return empty string after trimming
   207→**Rationale**: The trimming requirement specifies removing leading and trailing hyphens. If only hyphens remain after normalization, trimming all of them results in an empty string, consistent with other empty result scenarios.
   208→

     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→This feature provides a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs suitable for identifiers, filenames, and web URLs. The function normalizes text by converting it to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing special characters, and ensuring clean hyphen formatting.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→URL-safe slugs are a common requirement in web applications, content management systems, and data processing pipelines. A standardized slugify utility ensures consistent identifier generation across the codebase and reduces the risk of invalid characters in URLs, filenames, or database keys.
    18→
    19→## Functional Requirements
    20→
    21→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
    22→**Priority**: Must Have
    23→**User Type**: Developer
    24→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to convert input text to lowercase so that slugs are case-insensitive and consistent.
    25→
    26→**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization prevents duplicate identifiers that differ only in case (e.g., "Hello" vs "hello") and follows standard URL slug conventions.
    27→
    28→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    29→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    30→- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
    31→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case conversion
    32→- Example: "HELLO World" → "hello-world"
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
    35→**Priority**: Must Have
    36→**User Type**: Developer
    37→**Description**: As a developer, I need spaces and underscores in the input text to be replaced with hyphens so that slugs use a consistent word separator.
    38→
    39→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs and provide better readability than underscores or encoded spaces (%20).
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- All space characters (including multiple consecutive spaces) are replaced with hyphens
    43→- All underscore characters are replaced with hyphens
    44→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
    45→- Example: "hello  world" → "hello-world"
    46→- Example: "foo__bar" → "foo-bar"
    47→
    48→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal (Must Have)
    49→**Priority**: Must Have
    50→**User Type**: Developer
    51→**Description**: As a developer, I need special characters and punctuation to be removed from the slug so that the output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens.
    52→
    53→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, filenames, and database identifiers. Limiting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures broad compatibility.
    54→
    55→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    56→- Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) are retained in the output
    57→- All other characters (punctuation, symbols, etc.) are removed
    58→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world"
    59→- Example: "user@email.com" → "useremailcom"
    60→
    61→### REQ-004: Hyphen Normalization (Must Have)
    62→**Priority**: Must Have
    63→**User Type**: Developer
    64→**Description**: As a developer, I need multiple consecutive hyphens to be collapsed into a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.
    65→
    66→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can result from the combination of whitespace replacement and special character removal.
    67→
    68→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    69→- Any sequence of 2 or more consecutive hyphens is replaced with a single hyphen
    70→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
    71→- Example: "hello--world" → "hello-world"
    72→
    73→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
    74→**Priority**: Must Have
    75→**User Type**: Developer
    76→**Description**: As a developer, I need leading and trailing hyphens to be removed from the slug so that the output starts and ends with alphanumeric characters.
    77→
    78→**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at the beginning or end of input text and create invalid or unprofessional-looking identifiers.
    79→
    80→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    81→- Any hyphens at the start of the slug are removed
    82→- Any hyphens at the end of the slug are removed
    83→- Internal hyphens (between words) are preserved
    84→- Example: "-hello-world-" → "hello-world"
    85→- Example: "  foo bar  " → "foo-bar" (spaces become hyphens, then trimmed)
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Empty Input Handling (Must Have)
    88→**Priority**: Must Have
    89→**User Type**: Developer
    90→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to handle empty or whitespace-only input predictably so that the application doesn't fail when processing edge cases.
    91→
    92→**Rationale**: Empty input or input consisting only of special characters could result in an empty slug after processing, which needs to be handled gracefully.
    93→
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Empty string input returns an empty string
    96→- Input consisting only of whitespace returns an empty string
    97→- Input consisting only of special characters returns an empty string
    98→- Example: "" → ""
    99→- Example: "   " → ""
   100→- Example: "!!!" → ""
   101→
   102→## User Stories
   103→
   104→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title
   105→**As a** content management system developer
   106→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   107→**So that** articles have clean, readable URLs without manual slug creation
   108→
   109→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   110→- **GIVEN** an article title like "10 Best Practices for TypeScript"
   111→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("10 Best Practices for TypeScript")`
   112→- **THEN** I receive "10-best-practices-for-typescript"
   113→
   114→### STORY-002: Create Filename from User Input
   115→**As a** file processing system developer
   116→**I want** to sanitize user-provided names into valid filenames
   117→**So that** files can be saved without filesystem errors
   118→
   119→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   120→- **GIVEN** user input like "My Document (Final).txt"
   121→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("My Document (Final)")`
   122→- **THEN** I receive "my-document-final" suitable for a filename
   123→
   124→### STORY-003: Generate Database Identifier
   125→**As a** database system developer
   126→**I want** to create unique identifiers from human-readable names
   127→**So that** records have consistent, predictable keys
   128→
   129→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   130→- **GIVEN** a category name like "Home & Garden"
   131→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Home & Garden")`
   132→- **THEN** I receive "home-garden" suitable as a database key
   133→
   134→## Test Scenarios
   135→
   136→| Scenario | Input | Expected Output |
   137→|----------|-------|-----------------|
   138→| Basic text | "Hello World" | "hello-world" |
   139→| With punctuation | "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" |
   140→| Multiple spaces | "foo  bar" | "foo-bar" |
   141→| Underscores | "foo__bar" | "foo-bar" |
   142→| Leading/trailing spaces | "  foo bar  " | "foo-bar" |
   143→| Multiple hyphens | "a---b" | "a-b" |
   144→| Mixed case | "CamelCaseText" | "camelcasetext" |
   145→| Numbers | "test123" | "test123" |
   146→| Special characters | "user@email.com" | "useremailcom" |
   147→| Empty string | "" | "" |
   148→| Only spaces | "   " | "" |
   149→| Only special chars | "!!!" | "" |
   150→
   151→## Non-Functional Requirements
   152→
   153→### NFR-001: Performance
   154→The function should process typical input strings (< 1000 characters) in under 1ms on modern hardware.
   155→
   156→### NFR-002: Compatibility
   157→The function should work with standard JavaScript/TypeScript string types and return standard string output.
   158→
   159→### NFR-003: Testability
   160→The function should be a pure function (no side effects) that is easily testable with standard testing frameworks.
   161→
   162→## Out of Scope
   163→
   164→The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
   165→
   166→- Unicode character transliteration (e.g., "café" → "cafe")
   167→- Locale-specific character handling
   168→- Custom slug patterns or configurations
   169→- Maximum length enforcement
   170→- Uniqueness validation or collision detection
   171→- Persistence or caching of generated slugs
   172→
   173→## Dependencies
   174→

   176→- String manipulation capabilities (standard library)

   183→
   184→### Decision 1: PRD Association
   185→**Point**: PRD selection

   192→**Rationale**: The requirement specified "letter, number, or hyphen" without mentioning Unicode support. For a utility project, ASCII-only scope is the conservative default to avoid complexity around Unicode normalization and character classification.

    17→URL-safe slugs are a common requirement in web applications, content management systems, and data processing pipelines. A standardized slugify utility ensures consistent identifier generation across the codebase and reduces the risk of invalid characters in URLs, filenames, or database keys.
    18→
    19→## Functional Requirements
    20→
    21→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
    22→**Priority**: Must Have
    23→**User Type**: Developer
    24→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to convert input text to lowercase so that slugs are case-insensitive and consistent.
    25→
    26→**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization prevents duplicate identifiers that differ only in case (e.g., "Hello" vs "hello") and follows standard URL slug conventions.
    27→
    28→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    29→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    30→- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
    31→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case conversion
    32→- Example: "HELLO World" → "hello-world"
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
    35→**Priority**: Must Have
    36→**User Type**: Developer
    37→**Description**: As a developer, I need spaces and underscores in the input text to be replaced with hyphens so that slugs use a consistent word separator.
    38→
    39→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs and provide better readability than underscores or encoded spaces (%20).
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- All space characters (including multiple consecutive spaces) are replaced with hyphens
    43→- All underscore characters are replaced with hyphens
    44→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
    45→- Example: "hello  world" → "hello-world"
    46→- Example: "foo__bar" → "foo-bar"
    47→
    48→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal (Must Have)
    49→**Priority**: Must Have
    50→**User Type**: Developer
    51→**Description**: As a developer, I need special characters and punctuation to be removed from the slug so that the output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens.
    52→
    53→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, filenames, and database identifiers. Limiting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures broad compatibility.
    54→
    55→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    56→- Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) are retained in the output
    57→- All other characters (punctuation, symbols, etc.) are removed
    58→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world"
    59→- Example: "user@email.com" → "useremailcom"
    60→
    61→### REQ-004: Hyphen Normalization (Must Have)
    62→**Priority**: Must Have
    63→**User Type**: Developer
    64→**Description**: As a developer, I need multiple consecutive hyphens to be collapsed into a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.
    65→
    66→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can result from the combination of whitespace replacement and special character removal.
    67→
    68→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    69→- Any sequence of 2 or more consecutive hyphens is replaced with a single hyphen
    70→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
    71→- Example: "hello--world" → "hello-world"
    72→
    73→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
    74→**Priority**: Must Have
    75→**User Type**: Developer
    76→**Description**: As a developer, I need leading and trailing hyphens to be removed from the slug so that the output starts and ends with alphanumeric characters.
    77→
    78→**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at the beginning or end of input text and create invalid or unprofessional-looking identifiers.
    79→
    80→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    81→- Any hyphens at the start of the slug are removed
    82→- Any hyphens at the end of the slug are removed
    83→- Internal hyphens (between words) are preserved
    84→- Example: "-hello-world-" → "hello-world"
    85→- Example: "  foo bar  " → "foo-bar" (spaces become hyphens, then trimmed)
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Empty Input Handling (Must Have)
    88→**Priority**: Must Have
    89→**User Type**: Developer
    90→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to handle empty or whitespace-only input predictably so that the application doesn't fail when processing edge cases.
    91→
    92→**Rationale**: Empty input or input consisting only of special characters could result in an empty slug after processing, which needs to be handled gracefully.
    93→
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Empty string input returns an empty string
    96→- Input consisting only of whitespace returns an empty string
    97→- Input consisting only of special characters returns an empty string
    98→- Example: "" → ""
    99→- Example: "   " → ""
   100→- Example: "!!!" → ""
   101→
   102→## User Stories
   103→
   104→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title
   105→**As a** content management system developer
   106→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   107→**So that** articles have clean, readable URLs without manual slug creation
   108→
   109→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   110→- **GIVEN** an article title like "10 Best Practices for TypeScript"
   111→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("10 Best Practices for TypeScript")`
   112→- **THEN** I receive "10-best-practices-for-typescript"
   113→
   114→### STORY-002: Create Filename from User Input
   115→**As a** file processing system developer
   116→**I want** to sanitize user-provided names into valid filenames
   117→**So that** files can be saved without filesystem errors
   118→
   119→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   120→- **GIVEN** user input like "My Document (Final).txt"
   121→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("My Document (Final)")`
   122→- **THEN** I receive "my-document-final" suitable for a filename
   123→
   124→### STORY-003: Generate Database Identifier
   125→**As a** database system developer
   126→**I want** to create unique identifiers from human-readable names
   127→**So that** records have consistent, predictable keys
   128→
   129→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   130→- **GIVEN** a category name like "Home & Garden"
   131→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Home & Garden")`
   132→- **THEN** I receive "home-garden" suitable as a database key
   133→
   134→## Test Scenarios
   135→
   136→| Scenario | Input | Expected Output |
   137→|----------|-------|-----------------|
   138→| Basic text | "Hello World" | "hello-world" |
   139→| With punctuation | "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" |
   140→| Multiple spaces | "foo  bar" | "foo-bar" |
   141→| Underscores | "foo__bar" | "foo-bar" |
   142→| Leading/trailing spaces | "  foo bar  " | "foo-bar" |
   143→| Multiple hyphens | "a---b" | "a-b" |
   144→| Mixed case | "CamelCaseText" | "camelcasetext" |
   145→| Numbers | "test123" | "test123" |
   146→| Special characters | "user@email.com" | "useremailcom" |
   147→| Empty string | "" | "" |
   148→| Only spaces | "   " | "" |
   149→| Only special chars | "!!!" | "" |
   150→
   151→## Non-Functional Requirements
   152→
   153→### NFR-001: Performance
   154→The function should process typical input strings (< 1000 characters) in under 1ms on modern hardware.
   155→
   156→### NFR-002: Compatibility
   157→The function should work with standard JavaScript/TypeScript string types and return standard string output.
   158→
   159→### NFR-003: Testability
   160→The function should be a pure function (no side effects) that is easily testable with standard testing frameworks.
   161→
   162→## Out of Scope
   163→
   164→The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
   165→
   166→- Unicode character transliteration (e.g., "café" → "cafe")
   167→- Locale-specific character handling
   168→- Custom slug patterns or configurations
   169→- Maximum length enforcement
   170→- Uniqueness validation or collision detection
   171→- Persistence or caching of generated slugs
   172→
   173→## Dependencies
   174→
   175→- TypeScript/JavaScript runtime environment
   176→- String manipulation capabilities (standard library)
   177→
   178→## AFK Mode Decisions
   179→
   180→**AFK Mode**: Enabled
   181→
   182→The following decisions were made automatically based on project context:
   183→
   184→### Decision 1: PRD Association
   185→**Point**: PRD selection
   186→**Choice**: No PRD associated
   187→**Rationale**: No PRD documents found in `/tmp/rp1-evals/4b3c8c55/workspace/.rp1/work/prds/`. This appears to be a standalone utility feature request.
   188→
   189→### Decision 2: Character Set Scope
   190→**Point**: Allowed character definition
   191→**Choice**: ASCII alphanumeric (a-z, 0-9) and hyphens only
   192→**Rationale**: The requirement specified "letter, number, or hyphen" without mentioning Unicode support. For a utility project, ASCII-only scope is the conservative default to avoid complexity around Unicode normalization and character classification.
   193→
   194→### Decision 3: Empty Result Handling
   195→**Point**: Behavior when all characters are removed
   196→**Choice**: Return empty string
   197→**Rationale**: No specific error handling was requested. Returning an empty string is the natural result of the specified transformation rules and allows calling code to decide how to handle empty slugs.
   198→
   199→### Decision 4: Module Location
   200→**Point**: Implementation location
   201→**Choice**: Add to existing `src/utils.ts` module
   202→**Rationale**: The KB describes `src/utils.ts` as the location for "pure functions providing reusable logic," which matches the slugify function's nature. This maintains consistency with existing project structure.
   203→
   204→### Decision 5: Edge Case - Only Hyphens
   205→**Point**: Input that becomes only hyphens (e.g., "---")
   206→**Choice**: Return empty string after trimming
   207→**Rationale**: The trimming requirement specifies removing leading and trailing hyphens. If only hyphens remain after normalization, trimming all of them results in an empty string, consistent with other empty result scenarios.

# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility

## Overview

This feature provides a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs suitable for identifiers, filenames, and web URLs. The function normalizes text by converting it to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing special characters, and ensuring clean hyphen formatting.

## Business Context

URL-safe slugs are a common requirement in web applications, content management systems, and data processing pipelines. A standardized slugify utility ensures consistent identifier generation across the codebase and reduces the risk of invalid characters in URLs, filenames, or database keys.

## Functional Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to convert input text to lowercase so that slugs are case-insensitive and consistent.

**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization prevents duplicate identifiers that differ only in case (e.g., "Hello" vs "hello") and follows standard URL slug conventions.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case conversion
- Example: "HELLO World" → "hello-world"

### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: As a developer, I need spaces and underscores in the input text to be replaced with hyphens so that slugs use a consistent word separator.

**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs and provide better readability than underscores or encoded spaces (%20).

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- All space characters (including multiple consecutive spaces) are replaced with hyphens
- All underscore characters are replaced with hyphens
- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
- Example: "hello  world" → "hello-world"
- Example: "foo__bar" → "foo-bar"

### REQ-003: Special Character Removal (Must Have)
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: As a developer, I need special characters and punctuation to be removed from the slug so that the output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens.

**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, filenames, and database identifiers. Limiting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures broad compatibility.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) are retained in the output
- All other characters (punctuation, symbols, etc.) are removed
- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world"
- Example: "user@email.com" → "useremailcom"

### REQ-004: Hyphen Normalization (Must Have)
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: As a developer, I need multiple consecutive hyphens to be collapsed into a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.

**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can result from the combination of whitespace replacement and special character removal.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Any sequence of 2 or more consecutive hyphens is replaced with a single hyphen
- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
- Example: "hello--world" → "hello-world"

### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: As a developer, I need leading and trailing hyphens to be removed from the slug so that the output starts and ends with alphanumeric characters.

**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at the beginning or end of input text and create invalid or unprofessional-looking identifiers.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Any hyphens at the start of the slug are removed
- Any hyphens at the end of the slug are removed
- Internal hyphens (between words) are preserved
- Example: "-hello-world-" → "hello-world"
- Example: "  foo bar  " → "foo-bar" (spaces become hyphens, then trimmed)

### REQ-006: Empty Input Handling (Must Have)
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to handle empty or whitespace-only input predictably so that the application doesn't fail when processing edge cases.

**Rationale**: Empty input or input consisting only of special characters could result in an empty slug after processing, which needs to be handled gracefully.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Empty string input returns an empty string
- Input consisting only of whitespace returns an empty string
- Input consisting only of special characters returns an empty string
- Example: "" → ""
- Example: "   " → ""
- Example: "!!!" → ""

## User Stories

### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title
**As a** content management system developer
**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
**So that** articles have clean, readable URLs without manual slug creation

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- **GIVEN** an article title like "10 Best Practices for TypeScript"
- **WHEN** I call `slugify("10 Best Practices for TypeScript")`
- **THEN** I receive "10-best-practices-for-typescript"

### STORY-002: Create Filename from User Input
**As a** file processing system developer
**I want** to sanitize user-provided names into valid filenames
**So that** files can be saved without filesystem errors

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- **GIVEN** user input like "My Document (Final).txt"
- **WHEN** I call `slugify("My Document (Final)")`
- **THEN** I receive "my-document-final" suitable for a filename

### STORY-003: Generate Database Identifier
**As a** database system developer
**I want** to create unique identifiers from human-readable names
**So that** records have consistent, predictable keys

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- **GIVEN** a category name like "Home & Garden"
- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Home & Garden")`
- **THEN** I receive "home-garden" suitable as a database key

## Test Scenarios

| Scenario | Input | Expected Output |
|----------|-------|-----------------|
| Basic text | "Hello World" | "hello-world" |
| With punctuation | "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" |
| Multiple spaces | "foo  bar" | "foo-bar" |
| Underscores | "foo__bar" | "foo-bar" |
| Leading/trailing spaces | "  foo bar  " | "foo-bar" |
| Multiple hyphens | "a---b" | "a-b" |
| Mixed case | "CamelCaseText" | "camelcasetext" |
| Numbers | "test123" | "test123" |
| Special characters | "user@email.com" | "useremailcom" |
| Empty string | "" | "" |
| Only spaces | "   " | "" |
| Only special chars | "!!!" | "" |

## Non-Functional Requirements

### NFR-001: Performance
The function should process typical input strings (< 1000 characters) in under 1ms on modern hardware.

### NFR-002: Compatibility
The function should work with standard JavaScript/TypeScript string types and return standard string output.

### NFR-003: Testability
The function should be a pure function (no side effects) that is easily testable with standard testing frameworks.

## Out of Scope

The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:

- Unicode character transliteration (e.g., "café" → "cafe")
- Locale-specific character handling
- Custom slug patterns or configurations
- Maximum length enforcement
- Uniqueness validation or collision detection
- Persistence or caching of generated slugs

## Dependencies

- TypeScript/JavaScript runtime environment
- String manipulation capabilities (standard library)

## AFK Mode Decisions

**AFK Mode**: Enabled

The following decisions were made automatically based on project context:

### Decision 1: PRD Association
**Point**: PRD selection
**Choice**: No PRD associated
**Rationale**: No PRD documents found in `/tmp/rp1-evals/4b3c8c55/workspace/.rp1/work/prds/`. This appears to be a standalone utility feature request.

### Decision 2: Character Set Scope
**Point**: Allowed character definition
**Choice**: ASCII alphanumeric (a-z, 0-9) and hyphens only
**Rationale**: The requirement specified "letter, number, or hyphen" without mentioning Unicode support. For a utility project, ASCII-only scope is the conservative default to avoid complexity around Unicode normalization and character classification.

### Decision 3: Empty Result Handling
**Point**: Behavior when all characters are removed
**Choice**: Return empty string
**Rationale**: No specific error handling was requested. Returning an empty string is the natural result of the specified transformation rules and allows calling code to decide how to handle empty slugs.

### Decision 4: Module Location
**Point**: Implementation location
**Choice**: Add to existing `src/utils.ts` module
**Rationale**: The KB describes `src/utils.ts` as the location for "pure functions providing reusable logic," which matches the slugify function's nature. This maintains consistency with existing project structure.

### Decision 5: Edge Case - Only Hyphens
**Point**: Input that becomes only hyphens (e.g., "---")
**Choice**: Return empty string after trimming
**Rationale**: The trimming requirement specifies removing leading and trailing hyphens. If only hyphens remain after normalization, trimming all of them results in an empty string, consistent with other empty result scenarios.

# Design: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-07-04

## Summary

Implement a pure `slugify` function in `src/utils.ts` that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs using a chain of string transformations: lowercase conversion, whitespace/underscore replacement with hyphens, special character removal, hyphen collapse, and edge trimming. This approach follows existing codebase patterns for utility functions and requires no external dependencies, keeping the implementation simple and testable.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Input String"] --> Lower["toLowerCase()"]
    Lower --> Replace["Replace spaces/underscores with hyphens"]
    Replace --> Remove["Remove non-alphanumeric except hyphens"]
    Remove --> Collapse["Collapse consecutive hyphens"]
    Collapse --> Trim["Trim leading/trailing hyphens"]
    Trim --> Output["Output Slug"]
```

## Contracts

| Contract | Producer | Consumer | Required Fields Or Outputs |
|----------|----------|----------|----------------------------|
| slugify function | utils.ts | Any importing module | `(input: string) => string` - accepts any string, returns URL-safe slug |

## Component Plan

| # | Component | Description | Files Changed |
|---|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| T1 | slugify function | Pure function implementing the slug transformation pipeline: lowercase, replace whitespace/underscores, remove special chars, collapse hyphens, trim edges | src/utils.ts |
| T2 | slugify tests | Comprehensive test suite covering all requirements and edge cases from test scenarios | src/utils.test.ts |

## Implementation DAG

**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):

1. [T1] - Core implementation has no prerequisites

**Dependencies**:

- T2 -> T1 (Interface: tests import and call the slugify function)

**Critical Path**: T1 -> T2

## Validation Plan

| Behavior Or Contract | Failure Mode Covered | Test Type | Evidence Or Command |
|----------------------|----------------------|-----------|---------------------|
| Lowercase conversion (REQ-001) | Uppercase letters not converted | unit | `bun test` - "HELLO World" -> "hello-world" |

| Special char removal (REQ-003) | Invalid chars in output | unit | `bun test` - "Hello, World!", "user@email.com" cases |
| Hyphen collapse (REQ-004) | Multiple consecutive hyphens | unit | `bun test` - "a---b" -> "a-b" |
| Hyphen trimming (REQ-005) | Leading/trailing hyphens | unit | `bun test` - "-hello-world-" -> "hello-world" |
| Empty input handling (REQ-006) | Function throws or returns unexpected | unit | `bun test` - "", "   ", "!!!" cases |
| Performance (NFR-001) | Slow execution | manual | Typical inputs < 1000 chars process in < 1ms |

## Documentation Impact

| Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale |
|------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| edit | modules.md | Utils module | modules.md:utils | Add slugify to documented utility functions |

## Open Risks

# Design Decisions: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Created**: 2026-07-04

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | Implementation approach | Chain of string method calls and regex | Readable, maintainable, follows existing utils.ts patterns; no external dependencies needed | Single complex regex (less readable), external library like slugify npm (unnecessary dependency) |
| D2 | Transformation order | lowercase -> replace spaces/underscores -> remove special chars -> collapse hyphens -> trim | Logical pipeline where each step builds on previous; trimming last ensures clean output | Different ordering could produce different intermediate states but same result |
| D3 | Regex for special char removal | `/[^a-z0-9-]/g` | Simple, clear pattern matching ASCII alphanumeric and hyphens; operates after lowercase so only lowercase letters needed | Character class with ranges for upper and lowercase (more complex) |
| D4 | Hyphen collapse pattern | `/--+/g` | Matches two or more consecutive hyphens for replacement with single; more efficient than repeated single replacement | While loop with single replacement (slower), recursive approach (unnecessary complexity) |
| D5 | Edge trimming approach | Regex `/^-+|-+$/g` | Single regex handles both leading and trailing in one pass | Separate trim operations, substring manipulation (more verbose) |

---

## AFK Mode: Auto-Selected Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Source | Rationale |
|----------|--------|--------|-----------|
| Module location | src/utils.ts | KB modules.md | Documented as location for pure reusable utility functions |
| Function naming | camelCase `slugify` | KB patterns.md | Project naming convention for functions |
| Test structure | describe/test/expect in utils.test.ts | KB patterns.md, existing code | Bun test runner pattern used by existing tests |
| Documentation style | JSDoc comments | Existing codebase | Matches existing greet() and add() function documentation |
| Character set scope | ASCII alphanumeric only | Requirements AFK decision | Conservative default avoiding Unicode complexity |
| Empty result handling | Return empty string | Requirements AFK decision | Natural result of transformation rules |

     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→This feature provides a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs suitable for identifiers, filenames, and web URLs. The function normalizes text by converting it to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing special characters, and ensuring clean hyphen formatting.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→URL-safe slugs are a common requirement in web applications, content management systems, and data processing pipelines. A standardized slugify utility ensures consistent identifier generation across the codebase and reduces the risk of invalid characters in URLs, filenames, or database keys.
    18→
    19→## Functional Requirements
    20→
    21→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
    22→**Priority**: Must Have
    23→**User Type**: Developer
    24→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to convert input text to lowercase so that slugs are case-insensitive and consistent.
    25→
    26→**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization prevents duplicate identifiers that differ only in case (e.g., "Hello" vs "hello") and follows standard URL slug conventions.
    27→
    28→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    29→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    30→- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
    31→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case conversion
    32→- Example: "HELLO World" → "hello-world"
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
    35→**Priority**: Must Have
    36→**User Type**: Developer
    37→**Description**: As a developer, I need spaces and underscores in the input text to be replaced with hyphens so that slugs use a consistent word separator.
    38→
    39→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs and provide better readability than underscores or encoded spaces (%20).
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- All space characters (including multiple consecutive spaces) are replaced with hyphens
    43→- All underscore characters are replaced with hyphens
    44→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
    45→- Example: "hello  world" → "hello-world"
    46→- Example: "foo__bar" → "foo-bar"
    47→
    48→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal (Must Have)
    49→**Priority**: Must Have
    50→**User Type**: Developer
    51→**Description**: As a developer, I need special characters and punctuation to be removed from the slug so that the output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens.
    52→
    53→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, filenames, and database identifiers. Limiting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures broad compatibility.
    54→
    55→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    56→- Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) are retained in the output
    57→- All other characters (punctuation, symbols, etc.) are removed
    58→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world"
    59→- Example: "user@email.com" → "useremailcom"
    60→
    61→### REQ-004: Hyphen Normalization (Must Have)
    62→**Priority**: Must Have
    63→**User Type**: Developer
    64→**Description**: As a developer, I need multiple consecutive hyphens to be collapsed into a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.
    65→
    66→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can result from the combination of whitespace replacement and special character removal.
    67→
    68→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    69→- Any sequence of 2 or more consecutive hyphens is replaced with a single hyphen
    70→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
    71→- Example: "hello--world" → "hello-world"
    72→
    73→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
    74→**Priority**: Must Have
    75→**User Type**: Developer
    76→**Description**: As a developer, I need leading and trailing hyphens to be removed from the slug so that the output starts and ends with alphanumeric characters.
    77→
    78→**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at the beginning or end of input text and create invalid or unprofessional-looking identifiers.
    79→
    80→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    81→- Any hyphens at the start of the slug are removed
    82→- Any hyphens at the end of the slug are removed
    83→- Internal hyphens (between words) are preserved
    84→- Example: "-hello-world-" → "hello-world"
    85→- Example: "  foo bar  " → "foo-bar" (spaces become hyphens, then trimmed)
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Empty Input Handling (Must Have)
    88→**Priority**: Must Have
    89→**User Type**: Developer
    90→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to handle empty or whitespace-only input predictably so that the application doesn't fail when processing edge cases.
    91→
    92→**Rationale**: Empty input or input consisting only of special characters could result in an empty slug after processing, which needs to be handled gracefully.
    93→
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Empty string input returns an empty string
    96→- Input consisting only of whitespace returns an empty string
    97→- Input consisting only of special characters returns an empty string
    98→- Example: "" → ""
    99→- Example: "   " → ""

   104→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title
   105→**As a** content management system developer

The function normalizes text by converting it to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing special characters, and ensuring clean hyphen formatting.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→URL-safe slugs are a common requirement in web applications, content management systems, and data processing pipelines. A standardized slugify utility ensures consistent identifier generation across the codebase and reduces the risk of invalid characters in URLs, filenames, or database keys.
    18→
    19→## Functional Requirements
    20→
    21→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
    22→**Priority**: Must Have
    23→**User Type**: Developer
    24→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to convert input text to lowercase so that slugs are case-insensitive and consistent.
    25→
    26→**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization prevents duplicate identifiers that differ only in case (e.g., "Hello" vs "hello") and follows standard URL slug conventions.
    27→
    28→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    29→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    30→- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
    31→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case conversion
    32→- Example: "HELLO World" → "hello-world"
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
    35→**Priority**: Must Have
    36→**User Type**: Developer
    37→**Description**: As a developer, I need spaces and underscores in the input text to be replaced with hyphens so that slugs use a consistent word separator.
    38→
    39→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs and provide better readability than underscores or encoded spaces (%20).
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- All space characters (including multiple consecutive spaces) are replaced with hyphens
    43→- All underscore characters are replaced with hyphens
    44→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
    45→- Example: "hello  world" → "hello-world"
    46→- Example: "foo__bar" → "foo-bar"
    47→
    48→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal (Must Have)
    49→**Priority**: Must Have
    50→**User Type**: Developer
    51→**Description**: As a developer, I need special characters and punctuation to be removed from the slug so that the output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens.
    52→
    53→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, filenames, and database identifiers. Limiting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures broad compatibility.
    54→
    55→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    56→- Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) are retained in the output
    57→- All other characters (punctuation, symbols, etc.) are removed
    58→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world"
    59→- Example: "user@email.com" → "useremailcom"
    60→
    61→### REQ-004: Hyphen Normalization (Must Have)
    62→**Priority**: Must Have
    63→**User Type**: Developer
    64→**Description**: As a developer, I need multiple consecutive hyphens to be collapsed into a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.
    65→
    66→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can result from the combination of whitespace replacement and special character removal.
    67→
    68→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    69→- Any sequence of 2 or more consecutive hyphens is replaced with a single hyphen
    70→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
    71→- Example: "hello--world" → "hello-world"
    72→
    73→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
    74→**Priority**: Must Have
    75→**User Type**: Developer
    76→**Description**: As a developer, I need leading and trailing hyphens to be removed from the slug so that the output starts and ends with alphanumeric characters.
    77→
    78→**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at the beginning or end of input text and create invalid or unprofessional-looking identifiers.
    79→
    80→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    81→- Any hyphens at the start of the slug are removed
    82→- Any hyphens at the end of the slug are removed
    83→- Internal hyphens (between words) are preserved
    84→- Example: "-hello-world-" → "hello-world"
    85→- Example: "  foo bar  " → "foo-bar" (spaces become hyphens, then trimmed)
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Empty Input Handling (Must Have)
    88→**Priority**: Must Have
    89→**User Type**: Developer
    90→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to handle empty or whitespace-only input predictably so that the application doesn't fail when processing edge cases.
    91→
    92→**Rationale**: Empty input or input consisting only of special characters could result in an empty slug after processing, which needs to be handled gracefully.
    93→
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Empty string input returns an empty string
    96→- Input consisting only of whitespace returns an empty string
    97→- Input consisting only of special characters returns an empty string
    98→- Example: "" → ""
    99→- Example: "   " → ""
   100→- Example: "!!!" → ""
   101→
   102→## User Stories
   103→
   104→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title
   105→**As a** content management system developer
   106→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   107→**So that** articles have clean, readable URLs without manual slug creation
   108→
   109→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   110→- **GIVEN** an article title like "10 Best Practices for TypeScript"
   111→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("10 Best Practices for TypeScript")`
   112→- **THEN** I receive "10-best-practices-for-typescript"
   113→
   114→### STORY-002: Create Filename from User Input
   115→**As a** file processing system developer
   116→**I want** to sanitize user-provided names into valid filenames
   117→**So that** files can be saved without filesystem errors
   118→
   119→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   120→- **GIVEN** user input like "My Document (Final).txt"
   121→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("My Document (Final)")`
   122→- **THEN** I receive "my-document-final" suitable for a filename
   123→
   124→### STORY-003: Generate Database Identifier
   125→**As a** database system developer
   126→**I want** to create unique identifiers from human-readable names
   127→**So that** records have consistent, predictable keys
   128→
   129→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   130→- **GIVEN** a category name like "Home & Garden"
   131→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Home & Garden")`
   132→- **THEN** I receive "home-garden" suitable as a database key
   133→
   134→## Test Scenarios

   136→| Scenario | Input | Expected Output |

   138→| Basic text | "Hello World" | "hello-world" |
   139→| With punctuation | "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" |
   140→| Multiple spaces | "foo  bar" | "foo-bar" |
   141→| Underscores | "foo__bar" | "foo-bar" |
   142→| Leading/trailing spaces | "  foo bar  " | "foo-bar" |
   143→| Multiple hyphens | "a---b" | "a-b" |
   144→| Mixed case | "CamelCaseText" | "camelcasetext" |
   145→| Numbers | "test123" | "test123" |
   146→| Special characters | "user@email.com" | "useremailcom" |
   147→| Empty string | "" | "" |
   148→| Only spaces | "   " | "" |
   149→| Only special chars | "!!!" | "" |
   150→
   151→## Non-Functional Requirements
   152→
   153→### NFR-001: Performance
   154→The function should process typical input strings (< 1000 characters) in under 1ms on modern hardware.
   155→
   156→### NFR-002: Compatibility
   157→The function should work with standard JavaScript/TypeScript string types and return standard string output.
   158→
   159→### NFR-003: Testability
   160→The function should be a pure function (no side effects) that is easily testable with standard testing frameworks.
   161→
   162→## Out of Scope
   163→
   164→The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
   165→
   166→- Unicode character transliteration (e.g., "café" → "cafe")
   167→- Locale-specific character handling
   168→- Custom slug patterns or configurations
   169→- Maximum length enforcement
   170→- Uniqueness validation or collision detection
   171→- Persistence or caching of generated slugs
   172→

   192→**Rationale**: The requirement specified "letter, number, or hyphen" without mentioning Unicode support. For a utility project, ASCII-only scope is the conservative default to avoid complexity around Unicode normalization and character classification.

   194→### Decision 3: Empty Result Handling
