/**
 * Add two numbers.
 */
export function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  return a + b;
}

/**
 * Converts arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs.
 *
 * Transforms input by:
 * - Converting to lowercase
 * - Replacing spaces and underscores with hyphens
 * - Removing special characters (keeping only alphanumeric and hyphens)
 * - Collapsing consecutive hyphens
 * - Trimming leading and trailing hyphens
 *
 * @param input - The text to convert to a slug
 * @returns A URL-safe slug string, or empty string if input is empty/invalid
 */
export function slugify(input: string): string {
  return input
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[\s_]+/g, '-')
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, '')
    .replace(/-+/g, '-')
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '');
}

     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→This feature provides a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs suitable for identifiers, filenames, and web URLs. The function normalizes text by converting it to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing special characters, and ensuring clean hyphen formatting.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→URL-safe slugs are a common requirement in web applications, content management systems, and data processing pipelines. A standardized slugify utility ensures consistent identifier generation across the codebase and reduces the risk of invalid characters in URLs, filenames, or database keys.
    18→
    19→## Functional Requirements
    20→
    21→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
    22→**Priority**: Must Have
    23→**User Type**: Developer
    24→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to convert input text to lowercase so that slugs are case-insensitive and consistent.
    25→
    26→**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization prevents duplicate identifiers that differ only in case (e.g., "Hello" vs "hello") and follows standard URL slug conventions.
    27→
    28→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    29→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    30→- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
    31→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case conversion
    32→- Example: "HELLO World" → "hello-world"
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
    35→**Priority**: Must Have
    36→**User Type**: Developer
    37→**Description**: As a developer, I need spaces and underscores in the input text to be replaced with hyphens so that slugs use a consistent word separator.
    38→
    39→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs and provide better readability than underscores or encoded spaces (%20).
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- All space characters (including multiple consecutive spaces) are replaced with hyphens
    43→- All underscore characters are replaced with hyphens
    44→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
    45→- Example: "hello  world" → "hello-world"
    46→- Example: "foo__bar" → "foo-bar"
    47→
    48→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal (Must Have)
    49→**Priority**: Must Have
    50→**User Type**: Developer
    51→**Description**: As a developer, I need special characters and punctuation to be removed from the slug so that the output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens.
    52→
    53→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, filenames, and database identifiers. Limiting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures broad compatibility.
    54→
    55→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    56→- Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) are retained in the output
    57→- All other characters (punctuation, symbols, etc.) are removed
    58→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world"
    59→- Example: "user@email.com" → "useremailcom"
    60→
    61→### REQ-004: Hyphen Normalization (Must Have)
    62→**Priority**: Must Have
    63→**User Type**: Developer
    64→**Description**: As a developer, I need multiple consecutive hyphens to be collapsed into a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.
    65→
    66→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can result from the combination of whitespace replacement and special character removal.
    67→
    68→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    69→- Any sequence of 2 or more consecutive hyphens is replaced with a single hyphen
    70→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
    71→- Example: "hello--world" → "hello-world"
    72→
    73→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
    74→**Priority**: Must Have
    75→**User Type**: Developer
    76→**Description**: As a developer, I need leading and trailing hyphens to be removed from the slug so that the output starts and ends with alphanumeric characters.
    77→
    78→**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at the beginning or end of input text and create invalid or unprofessional-looking identifiers.
    79→
    80→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    81→- Any hyphens at the start of the slug are removed
    82→- Any hyphens at the end of the slug are removed
    83→- Internal hyphens (between words) are preserved
    84→- Example: "-hello-world-" → "hello-world"
    85→- Example: "  foo bar  " → "foo-bar" (spaces become hyphens, then trimmed)
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Empty Input Handling (Must Have)
    88→**Priority**: Must Have
    89→**User Type**: Developer
    90→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to handle empty or whitespace-only input predictably so that the application doesn't fail when processing edge cases.
    91→
    92→**Rationale**: Empty input or input consisting only of special characters could result in an empty slug after processing, which needs to be handled gracefully.
    93→
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Empty string input returns an empty string
    96→- Input consisting only of whitespace returns an empty string
    97→- Input consisting only of special characters returns an empty string
    98→- Example: "" → ""
    99→- Example: "   " → ""
   100→- Example: "!!!" → ""
   101→
   102→## User Stories

   104→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title

   123→

   125→**As a** database system developer

   127→**So that** records have consistent, predictable keys
   128→
   129→**Acceptance Criteria**:

   153→### NFR-001: Performance

     8→
     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→This feature provides a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs suitable for identifiers, filenames, and web URLs. The function normalizes text by converting it to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing special characters, and ensuring clean hyphen formatting.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→URL-safe slugs are a common requirement in web applications, content management systems, and data processing pipelines. A standardized slugify utility ensures consistent identifier generation across the codebase and reduces the risk of invalid characters in URLs, filenames, or database keys.
    18→
    19→## Functional Requirements
    20→
    21→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
    22→**Priority**: Must Have
    23→**User Type**: Developer
    24→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to convert input text to lowercase so that slugs are case-insensitive and consistent.
    25→
    26→**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization prevents duplicate identifiers that differ only in case (e.g., "Hello" vs "hello") and follows standard URL slug conventions.
    27→
    28→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    29→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    30→- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
    31→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case conversion
    32→- Example: "HELLO World" → "hello-world"
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
    35→**Priority**: Must Have
    36→**User Type**: Developer
    37→**Description**: As a developer, I need spaces and underscores in the input text to be replaced with hyphens so that slugs use a consistent word separator.
    38→
    39→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs and provide better readability than underscores or encoded spaces (%20).
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- All space characters (including multiple consecutive spaces) are replaced with hyphens
    43→- All underscore characters are replaced with hyphens
    44→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
    45→- Example: "hello  world" → "hello-world"
    46→- Example: "foo__bar" → "foo-bar"
    47→
    48→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal (Must Have)
    49→**Priority**: Must Have
    50→**User Type**: Developer
    51→**Description**: As a developer, I need special characters and punctuation to be removed from the slug so that the output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens.
    52→
    53→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, filenames, and database identifiers. Limiting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures broad compatibility.
    54→
    55→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    56→- Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) are retained in the output
    57→- All other characters (punctuation, symbols, etc.) are removed
    58→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world"
    59→- Example: "user@email.com" → "useremailcom"
    60→
    61→### REQ-004: Hyphen Normalization (Must Have)
    62→**Priority**: Must Have
    63→**User Type**: Developer
    64→**Description**: As a developer, I need multiple consecutive hyphens to be collapsed into a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.
    65→
    66→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can result from the combination of whitespace replacement and special character removal.
    67→
    68→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    69→- Any sequence of 2 or more consecutive hyphens is replaced with a single hyphen
    70→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
    71→- Example: "hello--world" → "hello-world"
    72→
    73→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
    74→**Priority**: Must Have
    75→**User Type**: Developer
    76→**Description**: As a developer, I need leading and trailing hyphens to be removed from the slug so that the output starts and ends with alphanumeric characters.
    77→
    78→**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at the beginning or end of input text and create invalid or unprofessional-looking identifiers.
    79→
    80→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    81→- Any hyphens at the start of the slug are removed
    82→- Any hyphens at the end of the slug are removed
    83→- Internal hyphens (between words) are preserved
    84→- Example: "-hello-world-" → "hello-world"
    85→- Example: "  foo bar  " → "foo-bar" (spaces become hyphens, then trimmed)
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Empty Input Handling (Must Have)
    88→**Priority**: Must Have

     8→
     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→This feature provides a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs suitable for identifiers, filenames, and web URLs. The function normalizes text by converting it to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing special characters, and ensuring clean hyphen formatting.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→URL-safe slugs are a common requirement in web applications, content management systems, and data processing pipelines. A standardized slugify utility ensures consistent identifier generation across the codebase and reduces the risk of invalid characters in URLs, filenames, or database keys.
    18→
    19→## Functional Requirements
    20→
    21→### REQ-001: Text Normalization (Must Have)
    22→**Priority**: Must Have
    23→**User Type**: Developer
    24→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to convert input text to lowercase so that slugs are case-insensitive and consistent.
    25→
    26→**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization prevents duplicate identifiers that differ only in case (e.g., "Hello" vs "hello") and follows standard URL slug conventions.
    27→
    28→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    29→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    30→- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
    31→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case conversion
    32→- Example: "HELLO World" → "hello-world"
    33→
    34→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement (Must Have)
    35→**Priority**: Must Have
    36→**User Type**: Developer
    37→**Description**: As a developer, I need spaces and underscores in the input text to be replaced with hyphens so that slugs use a consistent word separator.
    38→
    39→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs and provide better readability than underscores or encoded spaces (%20).
    40→
    41→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    42→- All space characters (including multiple consecutive spaces) are replaced with hyphens
    43→- All underscore characters are replaced with hyphens
    44→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
    45→- Example: "hello  world" → "hello-world"
    46→- Example: "foo__bar" → "foo-bar"
    47→
    48→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal (Must Have)
    49→**Priority**: Must Have
    50→**User Type**: Developer
    51→**Description**: As a developer, I need special characters and punctuation to be removed from the slug so that the output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens.
    52→
    53→**Rationale**: Special characters can cause issues in URLs, filenames, and database identifiers. Limiting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures broad compatibility.
    54→
    55→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    56→- Only letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-) are retained in the output
    57→- All other characters (punctuation, symbols, etc.) are removed
    58→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world"
    59→- Example: "user@email.com" → "useremailcom"
    60→
    61→### REQ-004: Hyphen Normalization (Must Have)
    62→**Priority**: Must Have
    63→**User Type**: Developer
    64→**Description**: As a developer, I need multiple consecutive hyphens to be collapsed into a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.
    65→
    66→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can result from the combination of whitespace replacement and special character removal.
    67→
    68→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    69→- Any sequence of 2 or more consecutive hyphens is replaced with a single hyphen
    70→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
    71→- Example: "hello--world" → "hello-world"
    72→
    73→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming (Must Have)
    74→**Priority**: Must Have
    75→**User Type**: Developer
    76→**Description**: As a developer, I need leading and trailing hyphens to be removed from the slug so that the output starts and ends with alphanumeric characters.
    77→
    78→**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at the beginning or end of input text and create invalid or unprofessional-looking identifiers.
    79→
    80→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    81→- Any hyphens at the start of the slug are removed
    82→- Any hyphens at the end of the slug are removed
    83→- Internal hyphens (between words) are preserved
    84→- Example: "-hello-world-" → "hello-world"
    85→- Example: "  foo bar  " → "foo-bar" (spaces become hyphens, then trimmed)
    86→
    87→### REQ-006: Empty Input Handling (Must Have)
    88→**Priority**: Must Have
    89→**User Type**: Developer
    90→**Description**: As a developer, I need the slugify function to handle empty or whitespace-only input predictably so that the application doesn't fail when processing edge cases.
    91→
    92→**Rationale**: Empty input or input consisting only of special characters could result in an empty slug after processing, which needs to be handled gracefully.
    93→
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Empty string input returns an empty string
    96→- Input consisting only of whitespace returns an empty string
    97→- Input consisting only of special characters returns an empty string
    98→- Example: "" → ""
    99→- Example: "   " → ""
   100→- Example: "!!!" → ""
   101→
   102→## User Stories
   103→
   104→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from Title
   105→**As a** content management system developer
   106→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-safe slugs
   107→**So that** articles have clean, readable URLs without manual slug creation
   108→
   109→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   110→- **GIVEN** an article title like "10 Best Practices for TypeScript"
   111→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("10 Best Practices for TypeScript")`
   112→- **THEN** I receive "10-best-practices-for-typescript"
   113→
   114→### STORY-002: Create Filename from User Input
   115→**As a** file processing system developer
   116→**I want** to sanitize user-provided names into valid filenames
   117→**So that** files can be saved without filesystem errors
   118→
   119→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   120→- **GIVEN** user input like "My Document (Final).txt"
   121→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("My Document (Final)")`
   122→- **THEN** I receive "my-document-final" suitable for a filename
   123→
   124→### STORY-003: Generate Database Identifier
   125→**As a** database system developer
   126→**I want** to create unique identifiers from human-readable names
   127→**So that** records have consistent, predictable keys
   128→
   129→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   130→- **GIVEN** a category name like "Home & Garden"
   131→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Home & Garden")`
   132→- **THEN** I receive "home-garden" suitable as a database key
   133→
   134→## Test Scenarios
   135→
   136→| Scenario | Input | Expected Output |
   137→|----------|-------|-----------------|
   138→| Basic text | "Hello World" | "hello-world" |
   139→| With punctuation | "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" |
   140→| Multiple spaces | "foo  bar" | "foo-bar" |
   141→| Underscores | "foo__bar" | "foo-bar" |
   142→| Leading/trailing spaces | "  foo bar  " | "foo-bar" |
   143→| Multiple hyphens | "a---b" | "a-b" |
   144→| Mixed case | "CamelCaseText" | "camelcasetext" |
   145→| Numbers | "test123" | "test123" |
   146→| Special characters | "user@email.com" | "useremailcom" |
   147→| Empty string | "" | "" |
   148→| Only spaces | "   " | "" |
   149→| Only special chars | "!!!" | "" |
   150→
   151→## Non-Functional Requirements
   152→
   153→### NFR-001: Performance
   154→The function should process typical input strings (< 1000 characters) in under 1ms on modern hardware.
   155→
   156→### NFR-002: Compatibility
   157→The function should work with standard JavaScript/TypeScript string types and return standard string output.
   158→
   159→### NFR-003: Testability
   160→The function should be a pure function (no side effects) that is easily testable with standard testing frameworks.
   161→
   162→## Out of Scope
   163→
   164→The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
   165→
   166→- Unicode character transliteration (e.g., "café" → "cafe")
   167→- Locale-specific character handling
   168→- Custom slug patterns or configurations
   169→- Maximum length enforcement
   170→- Uniqueness validation or collision detection
   171→- Persistence or caching of generated slugs
   172→
   173→## Dependencies
   174→
   175→- TypeScript/JavaScript runtime environment
   176→- String manipulation capabilities (standard library)
   177→
   178→## AFK Mode Decisions
   179→
   180→**AFK Mode**: Enabled
   181→
   182→The following decisions were made automatically based on project context:
   183→
   184→### Decision 1: PRD Association
   185→**Point**: PRD selection
   186→**Choice**: No PRD associated
   187→**Rationale**: No PRD documents found in `/tmp/rp1-evals/4b3c8c55/workspace/.rp1/work/prds/`. This appears to be a standalone utility feature request.
   188→
   189→### Decision 2: Character Set Scope
   190→**Point**: Allowed character definition
   191→**Choice**: ASCII alphanumeric (a-z, 0-9) and hyphens only
   192→**Rationale**: The requirement specified "letter, number, or hyphen" without mentioning Unicode support. For a utility project, ASCII-only scope is the conservative default to avoid complexity around Unicode normalization and character classification.
   193→
   194→### Decision 3: Empty Result Handling
   195→**Point**: Behavior when all characters are removed
   196→**Choice**: Return empty string
   197→**Rationale**: No specific error handling was requested. Returning an empty string is the natural result of the specified transformation rules and allows calling code to decide how to handle empty slugs.
   198→
   199→### Decision 4: Module Location
   200→**Point**: Implementation location
   201→**Choice**: Add to existing `src/utils.ts` module
   202→**Rationale**: The KB describes `src/utils.ts` as the location for "pure functions providing reusable logic," which matches the slugify function's nature. This maintains consistency with existing project structure.
   203→
   204→### Decision 5: Edge Case - Only Hyphens
   205→**Point**: Input that becomes only hyphens (e.g., "---")
   206→**Choice**: Return empty string after trimming
   207→**Rationale**: The trimming requirement specifies removing leading and trailing hyphens. If only hyphens remain after normalization, trimming all of them results in an empty string, consistent with other empty result scenarios.
   208→
